plan.title: Opening cue
plan.action: Start with “Ella Fitzgerald” as the familiar cue, then branch toward “Jazz.” keep the pace gentle and low-pressure.
plan.why: The session starts from the supplied favorite “Ella Fitzgerald” and uses Qloo-ranked “Jazz” as adjacent cultural evidence.

plan.title: Story bridge
plan.action: Bridge from “Duke Ellington” into “swing” with a film scene, photo, lyric, or memory prompt. Keep it for a small group with room for individual responses.
plan.why: “Duke Ellington” is a supplied favorite; Qloo-ranked “swing” provides the adjacent cultural bridge instead of a generic nostalgia prompt.

plan.title: Shared choice
plan.action: Offer two or three simple choices connected to “piano” and let participants steer the next activity.
plan.why: “piano” extends the known tastes into a related domain while preserving participant choice.

plan.title: Closing ritual
plan.action: Close with a snack, sensory cue, or conversation card inspired by “Vocal-Jazz,” then ask what should return next time.
plan.why: “Vocal-Jazz” keeps the closing step grounded in selected Qloo evidence so the plan ends in the same cultural neighborhood it started in.

note: High-coherence same-domain comparison case. Retained for transparency; not the canonical judge demo because Aretha Franklin + The Sound of Music better demonstrates Qloo's cross-category value.
